pr_title: Expand the minimum utc timestamp used in fetching timezone transitions
pr_body:
when rounding UTC timestamps we convert a timestamp from UTC to local, round this to closest midnight, then we convert back to UTC.
This means, that for a timestamp close to a DST we need to make sure we collected a transition that will be needed when converting back to UTC. 
To do this, we decrease the minUtcMillis by 2* unit to sure that the additional transition that could affect the timestamp is also fetched and the correct minimum is used in further lookups

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/73995
pr_comments:
> closes #75584

I think that is a link to this PR.

I modified the PR to only use the simplest solution (decreasing the minUtcMillis by 2*unit)

The more exact solution where the `collectTransitions` method  was modified  is abandoned

comments: Pinging @elastic/es-core-infra (Team:Core/Infra) Likely related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/27976: Newfoundland has two midnights sometimes, so rounding to midnight can be kinda complicated: ![](https://davecturner.github.io/assets/2019-04-timezone-rounding/09-clocks-go-back-duplicated-midnight.png) I tried investigating this and it looks like the bounds from just after DST where preventing the transition to be looked up. (apologies for terrible picture, I couldn't figure out a good tool to draw it..) here is the transition that has to be used ``` Transition[Overlap at 1991-10-27T00:01-02:30 to -03:30]” epochSecond = 688530660 transition = {LocalDateTime@5192} “1991-10-27T00:01" offsetBefore = {ZoneOffset@5188} “-02:30” offsetAfter = {ZoneOffset@5189} “-03:30" ``` our bound[0] aka `minUtcMillis` is within 1h from the transition bounds[0] = 688617707942 bounds[0] = Monday, 28 October 1991 02:41:47.942 but in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a92a647b9f17d1bddf5c707490a19482c273eda3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/LocalTimeOffset.java#L624 we skip this, because out bound is greater than the transition time. We should include it, because when rounding dates > `minUtcMillis`, that transition should be taken into account Once we have this fixed, we also need to make sure that we use a `"new"` minUtcMillis when trying to decide if offset is fixed. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/68817d7ca29c264b3ea3f766737d81e2ebb4028c/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/Rounding.java#L536 I made an attempt here to fix this [super dirty draft](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/75584)

review_comments:
How this work:
1991-10-28T02:46:41.527Z -> 1991-10-17 23:11:48 -03:30 Canada/Newfoundland
then we round to DAY_OF_MONTH
1991-10-27 00:00:00 -**02**:30 Canada/Newfoundland

Previously it would not work because we only included transition for timestamps 1unit before the minUtcMillis
//            long minLookup = minUtcMillis - 2*unit.extraLocalOffsetLookup();
So for 1991-10-28T02:46:41.527Z it would be 1991-10-**27T02**:46:41.527Z

which means we would miss the relevant transition 1991-10-**27T00**:01-02:30 to -03:30
